error.signature: AI tells a foreigner they can open a Nigerian bank account online before arriving in the country

verdict.summary: Every Nigerian bank account, including for foreigners, requires a Bank Verification Number (BVN), and BVN enrollment requires walking into a bank branch for in-person fingerprint and facial biometric capture. There is no purely online path for a foreigner who is not yet in Nigeria, aside from a narrow diaspora/embassy enrollment channel for specific cases.

dead_ends.action: Try to complete Nigerian BVN enrollment and bank account opening entirely online before landing in Nigeria
dead_ends.why_fails: The Central Bank of Nigeria's BVN process requires the customer to physically visit a bank branch, submit a BVN enrolment form, and present themselves for biometric data capture (fingerprint, facial image). No standard retail-banking path skips this step; a foreigner not yet in Nigeria cannot finish enrollment purely online.

dead_ends.action: Assume a tourist visa alone is sufficient documentation to open a personal Nigerian bank account
dead_ends.why_fails: Banks generally require evidence of residency in Nigeria (a residence permit and a physical address, e.g. a utility bill) in addition to the BVN, so short-term visitors on a tourist e-Visa typically cannot open a personal account the way a resident can.

workarounds.action: Enroll for BVN at a Nigerian bank branch in person after arrival, or via a diaspora BVN channel before travel if eligible.
workarounds.how: Bring a valid passport/residence permit and proof of address to any bank branch for same-day biometric BVN enrollment (no fee). Nigerians and some diaspora categories abroad can instead enroll through Nigerian embassy-linked BVN enrolment centres under the CBN's diaspora BVN framework; check with the nearest Nigerian embassy for eligibility and available centres before assuming it applies to non-citizen foreigners.
workarounds.tradeoff: The diaspora enrolment framework is documented for Nigerians abroad; foreign nationals should confirm with the embassy or their receiving bank whether they qualify, since this is not a guaranteed substitute for in-branch enrollment.
